instance_recommendations.rationale: Best price-performance option. Same vCPU/memory as current c5.2xlarge but 10% cheaper. AMD EPYC (Milan) provides comparable or better single-thread performance for transcription workloads. Top recommendation for balanced strategy.
Second-best price-performance. AMD-based alternative nearly identical savings to c6a.2xlarge. Good fallback if c6a capacity is constrained in us-west-2.
Current baseline instance type. Intel Xeon Platinum, well-proven. No savings but zero migration risk.

Same price as c5.2xlarge but newer Intel Ice Lake architecture with ~15% better per-core performance. Effectively better price-performance at the same cost, useful if workload is CPU-bound on single-core throughput.

rationale.scaling_policy: Step thresholds are aligned with observed queue depth percentiles. The queue is at zero 77% of the time (p50=0), so the first step (0–10) aggressively scales down by 15 to shed idle capacity quickly during long quiet periods. The 10–80 range provides moderate scale-down (-5) to gently reduce capacity when the queue is non-zero but below typical working levels. Scale-up begins at 80 messages (near the original policy's first scale-up threshold), with +10 for the 80–225 band (p95=223.7), +30 for 225–1600 (covering the p95-to-p99 range where p99=1596.45), +60 for 1600–5000 for high-load bursts, and +120 for extreme spikes above 5000 (approaching the observed max of 6606). The aggressive top step ensures the ASG can ramp toward the observed peak desired capacity of 816 within a few scaling cycles even at extreme queue depths.
rationale.strategy_impact: Balanced strategy drove the selection of moderate cooldown (300s, matching the instance drain time) rather than an aggressive shorter cooldown. This prevents thrashing during the frequent zero-to-spike transitions visible in the data while still allowing responsive scale-up within ~5 minutes. Instance recommendations favor the best price-per-hour options (c6a, c5a) rather than the newest/fastest (c7i, c8i) since the workload already scales horizontally to 800+ instances — marginal per-instance performance gains don't justify 5–27% higher costs. The step sizes balance queue drain speed against over-provisioning cost.
rationale.risk_notes: 1) The 300s cooldown means during extreme bursts the ASG can only adjust every 5 minutes; given max observed queue depth of ~6600 and peak desired of 816 instances, it may take 2-3 scaling cycles (10-15 min) to fully scale up from a cold start. Monitor p99 latency during burst onset. 2) Zero-depth percentage is 77.18% which is below the 80% threshold for recommending scale-to-zero, so min_size=1 is maintained. 3) Current policy has cooldown=0 which risks launching excessive instances before warmup completes; the recommended 300s cooldown may feel slower but prevents capacity overshoot and wasted spend. 4) If migrating to c6a.2xlarge, validate that transcription libraries have no Intel-specific optimizations (e.g., MKL, AVX-512) that would degrade on AMD; c6i.2xlarge is the safe Intel upgrade path if so.
